title: Finland – Repair and maintenance services – Kattohuoltopalvelut Kiinteistö Oy Auroranlinnan kiinteistöissä
description: Hankinnan kohteena ovat Kiinteistö oy Auroranlinnalle suoritettavat kattotarkastukset, pienkorjaukset ja akuutit tilaustyöt kiinteistöhuollon tai Auroranlinnan kautta. Auroranlinnalla on kiinteistöjä noin 80 kohteessa ympäri Helsinkiä. Kiinteistöt/yhtiöt ovat kooltaan paritaloista yli 160 asuntoa käsittäviin talokokonaisuuksiin. Tarjoajalla tulee siten olla riittävät resurssit töiden loppuun saattamiseksi. Tehtävään on tarkoitus valita urakoitsija, joka ovat saanut eniten pisteitä kilpailutuksesta. Kohteisiin voi tutustua Auroranlinnan nettisivujen kautta ja paikan päällä käymällä. Sopimus on tarkoitus alkaa 5.1.2027. Sopimus tehdään määräaikaisena 2 vuodeksi. Sopimukseen sisältyy optio (2) kahdesta yhden (1) vuoden pituisesta optiovuodesta.

title: Prototype development for Battlefield Wound Infection Prevention and Treatment (BWI P&T) Barrier Combination
description: This RPP is being issued by the Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), in support of the Defense Health Agency�s Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Medical Products (MP) Warfighter Protection (WPAC) & Acute Care Program Management Office (PMO) Care located in Frederick, Maryland at Fort Detrick. The Warfighter Protection and Acute Care Project Management Office (WPAC PMO) has a requirement for the development of a Barrier Combination product. The Barrier Combination product is defined as being composed of both a physical barrier to protect a wound and an antibacterial and/or antifungal activity released from the barrier to prevent the spread of organisms and avoid systemic infections. This RPP will result in one award to develop the Battlefield Wound Infection Prevention and Treatment (BWI P&T) Barrier Combination (BC) prototype product. The final product MUST be a combination wound treatment that includes a barrier component that is either infused or impregnated with antimicrobial and/or antifungal properties and have U.S. Food Drug Administration (FDA) approval (or clearance). The award, as a result of this RPP, will be awarded under the authority of prototype Other Transaction Authority (pOTA) 10 U.S.C. 4022.

title: Construction of Chilled Water Plant and Site Utility Upgrades at VA Medical Center in West Haven, CT
description: The scope of the chilled water plant replacement consists of the demolition of the existing chilled water plant (building 16a) and construction of a new multi-story chilled water plant to include chillers, cooling towers, pumps, and all associated mechanical and electrical equipment. Due to the close proximity of the existing fuel tank farm adjacent to the existing chilled water plant, a new fuel tank farm will need to be constructed as part of the project, which primarily serves the central boiler plant, requiring close coordination with the medical center and ongoing related projects.The scope of the site utility upgrades consists of the replacement and upgrade of the existing fire protection water main and the domestic water main from Campbell Avenue to Building 15. Site utility upgrades also include providing utility main loops of chilled water supply and return, steam supply, condensate return, domestic water supply, and fire protection water supply which will originate from the new chilled water plant and back-feed to Building 1. The work also includes the installation of redundant electrical feeder from the utility demarcation point to Building 19 and coordination with the local electrical utility provider to provide further electrical redundancy offsite as well. In addition, new water storage tanks will be constructed. This project involves civil/site, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural, geotechnical, and architectural disciplines. The project must also comply with the DVAs Physical Security Resiliency Design Requirements (PSRDM). It is expected that the chilled water plant will be constructed to meet USGBC LEED Silver certification. The work is located adjacent to and within an active Medical Center campus which will be operational at all times. Impact to on-going operations must be kept to a minimum and carefully coordinated with the Contracting Officer and VAMC staff. In addition, the work area is constrained due to the active medical center operations which will limit laydown and storage areas during construction.

title: Material Management
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation or request for proposal and no contract or purchase order will be awarded from this notice. There is no solicitation at this time. Military Sealift Command (MSC) is seeking information and potential contractors in support of an upcoming planned requirement in support of MSC�s Logistics Directorate (N4). The Contractor shall provide non-personal logistics services including Material Receipt; Material Stowage; Special Material Stowage; Material Transportation; Material Disposal; Special Materials, Centrally Managed Stock; Real-Time Reutilization Asset Management; Ashore Audit and Inventory; Customer Service; Material Handling Equipment and Warehouse Equipment; Training and Phase in and Phase out for MSC ashore locations worldwide. Additionally, the Contractor shall provide all required labor, travel, material, and vehicle support necessary to complete the requirement. MSC will provide warehouse and office space, including various forklifts and storage aids for the Contractor to provide the above-mentioned services. The anticipated period of performance is a one-year base period, plus four (4), one-year option periods with a total period of performance from 19 September 2027 � 18 September 2032. The anticipated NAICS Code is 493110: General Warehousing and Storage. This is a market research tool used to determine the availability and adequacy of potential business sources prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of an award. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources as a result of this notice. Respondents will not be notified of the results and the U.S. Government is not required to answer any questions submitted in regards to this notice. Please note the information within this notice will be updated and/or may change prior to an official synopsis/solicitation, if any. Sources Sought Submission Requirements: It is requested that interested businesses submit information outlining their company information, small business standing, ability to perform in accordance with the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS), and intent of subcontracting. Submission is not a prerequisite to any potential future offerings, but participation will assist the Government in tailoring the requirement to be consistent with industry. Responses should reference the Sources Sought Notice and shall include the following information in this format: (a) Company profile including number of employees, office location, Unique Entity ID, and CAGE Code. (b) Point of contact, telephone number, fax number, address, and email address (if available). (c) Corporate Experience and Management: Global Operations: Describe your company�s experience managing logistics and warehouse operations of similar size, scope, and complexity across multiple, geographically dispersed international locations as detailed in draft PWS Section 1.1. How do you ensure standardized performance and quality control across all sites? Key Personnel: The draft PWS identifies numerous key personnel with specific, high-level qualifications (PWS Section 3.20). Describe your strategy for recruiting, hiring, and retaining personnel who meet these stringent requirements for the life of the contract. What is your plan for rapidly filling vacancies to meet the 30-day requirement? Subcontractor Management: If applicable, describe your experience managing subcontractors to meet the requirements of a complex, global contract. How do you ensure subcontractors adhere to all performance, security, and quality standards outlined in the draft PWS? (d) Technical and Operational Capability: Inventory Management and Accuracy: The PWS requires maintaining a 98% inventory accuracy rate and conducting 100% annual inventories (PWS Section 3.2, 3.6). Describe your technical approach and quality control processes for achieving and sustaining this level of accuracy across the estimated workload, including your methodology for causative research of gains and losses. Logistics Modernization & System Integration: Section 3.10 outlines a significant requirement for advanced warehouse operations and logistics modernization, including data cleansing, and developing capabilities to be integrated with the government's system of record (CMLS, ERP plus or current system). Describe your experience in cleansing, normalizing, and standardizing large, disparate inventory data sets. Detail your capabilities and past performance in developing and integrating custom modules (e.g., material visibility, stowage optimization) with existing government or commercial Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems. Special Material Handling: This contract requires handling, stowing, and transporting various special materials, including Hazardous Material (HAZMAT), temperature-controlled items, and Security Risk Category (SRC) II-IV Small Arms (PWS Sections 3.2, 3.3). Please describe your experience, certifications, and established procedures for managing these materials in compliance with all cited regulations. Ship Decommissioning Support: Describe your experience providing logistics support for ship deactivation, to include embarking on vessels, as outlined in PWS section 3.4.2. Detail your ability to work within shipboard systems (e.g., ShipCLIP, eRMS) and manage the disposition of large volumes of material in a dynamic environment. Surge and Contingency Operations: The draft PWS requires the ability to surge to 24/7 operations during emergencies or contingencies (PWS Section 1.1.13). Describe your plan and capabilities for rapidly augmenting your workforce and resources to meet these demands at any of the specified global locations. Security: This contract requires a SECRET facility clearance and for personnel to have security clearances. Describe your company's experience in managing cleared contracts and personnel, including your processes for ensuring compliance with all security requirements outlined in PWS section 3.17, particularly the unique staffing requirements for South Korea. (d) Describe any past performance efforts with a similar scope to the proposed requirement. Provide contract numbers, dollar value, and the period of performance for each contract referenced in the response to this source sought notice. (e) Provide feedback on edits to the draft PWS or overall requirement, areas for innovative approaches, or other recommendations on the best ways to fulfill this requirement. Responses are requested, via email, prior to 1300 hours, Eastern Time, 23 October 2026. The point of contact is Jamiel Blizzard, email Jamiel.n.blizzard.civ@us.navy.mil

title: Palm Beach Harbor, South Jetty Rehabilitation 2026, Palm Beach County, Florida
description: The work consists of rehabilitation of the South Jetty at Palm Beach Harbor. Rehabilitation will require substantial moving and manipulation of both new and existing stones to obtain the required interlocking within the tolerances provided. Mobilization of equipment and the construction necessary to repair the jetty must be water-based and require the use of marine construction methods and equipment. Work on top of the jetty will be permitted. Land-based access to the project site will not be permitted. Rehabilitation also consists of concrete repairs to the South Jetty at Palm Beach Harbor as indicated on the drawings. Prior to work on the jetty, conduct a pre-construction benthic community survey on the jetty structure and any adjacent submerged areas that may be impacted by the Contractors operations. Complete any coral relocations required as a result of the benthic survey prior to jetty work. Field personnel conducting coral survey and transplantation activities must either be qualified relocation contractors by the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission or must provide documentation of having successfully conducted relocation of corals in Florida. The project will have an estimated period of performance of 330 calendar days after receipt of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). description: A Pre-Bid Conference will be held via teleconference on October 7, 2026 @ 10:00am EDT. The call-in number is: +1 601-262-2433, the Access Code is: 208 969 158#, Attendee ID: 993 907 442 865 / Passcode: bm7je2Mr and the link to be utilized is as follows: HTTPS://WWW.MICROSOFT.COM/EN-US/MICROSOFT-TEAMS/JOIN-A-MEETINGIt is requested that an email be sent to Guesley.Leger@usace.army.mil no later than October 5, 2026, at 04:00pm, EDT to confirm attendance by your organization. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: The work consists of rehabilitation of the South Jetty at Palm Beach Harbor. Rehabilitation will require substantial moving and manipulation of both new and existing stones to obtain the required interlocking within the tolerances provided. Mobilization of equipment and the construction necessary to repair the jetty must be water-based and require the use of marine construction methods and equipment. Work on top of the jetty will be permitted. Land-based access to the project site will not be permitted. Rehabilitation also consists of concrete repairs to the South Jetty at Palm Beach Harbor as indicated on the drawings. Prior to work on the jetty, conduct a pre-construction benthic community survey on the jetty structure and any adjacent submerged areas that may be impacted by the Contractors operations. Complete any coral relocations required as a result of the benthic survey prior to jetty work. Field personnel conducting coral survey and transplantation activities must either be qualified relocation contractors by the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission or must provide documentation of having successfully conducted relocation of corals in Florida. The project will have an estimated period of performance of 330 calendar days after receipt of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). The stated time is inclusive of 60 calendar days to commence work and will be divided into base work and three options as follows: The Estimated Magnitude of construction is between $1,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00The Invitation for Bid (IFB) will be issued on or about September 23, 2026 and bids will be due on or about October 23, 2026.THIS ACQUISITION REQUIRES THE USE OF COAST GUARD-CERTIFIED EQUIPMENT, The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. title: Methylphenidate ER
description: The Defense Logistics Agency is planning to issue a solicitation for a national requirements contract for Methylphenidate ER Tablets. Procurement details follow. Methylphenidate ER 18MG, 27MG, 36MG, and 54MG Tablets in 100 count bottles. This will be an unrestricted and fully competitive acquisition. The contract will be a firm-fixed price, requirements type contract with a one-year base and four one-year options. A contract resulting from this solicitation will establish a national supply source, in accordance with FAR 52.216-21 (Requirements), to provide the items listed in the schedule for purchase by Department of War, Department of Veterans Affairs, Indian Health Service and Bureau of Prisons customers through the DLA and VA prime vendor programs. The annual usage estimates will be provided in the Schedule of Supplies section of the solicitation. This is a commercial item and will be solicited using FAR part 12. All sources may submit a proposal which shall be considered by the agency. A copy of the solicitation will be posted to the DLA Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil and Sam.Gov at https://sam.gov. Interested parties should contact Jeremy Brown at (445) 737-5419, (jeremy.brown@dla.mil) for any questions/comments. The current projected solicitation date is September of 2026. DLA reserves the right to issue the solicitation before or after the projected solicitation date.

title: MODIFIED WC-130J RTP APN-241 WEATHER RADAR SUSTAINING ENGINEERING SUPPORT RESEARCH AND SUPPORT TASK
description: The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualifications to support repairability maintainability, and sustaining engineering for the modified WC-130J RTP APN-241 Weather Radar. Potential sources must possess the ability to provide engineering studies for the WC-130J RTP APN-241 system in resolving reliability and maintainability issues, obsolete parts issues, identify and propose solutions to Diminishing Manufacturing Sources (DMS) issues, and analyze failure trends from both the depots and the field level shops to support the MC-130J CR-2M developmental testing. For vendors wishing to participate in this Request for Information (RFI), after reviewing the requirement, provide documentation supporting proof of company�s capability to meet the requested requirements. If lacking sufficient experience/capabilities in a particular area, please provide details explaining strategies to overcome the lack of experience/capabilities to perform that portion of the requirement. In accordance with RFO 15.101(c), this RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This request for information does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or services. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses incurred in response to this RFI; all cost associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in future RFPs nor does it ensure participation, if an RFP is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Federal Business Opportunities (SAM.gov) website. It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this requirement. Potential sources must be able to install the APN-241 Weather radar in addition to troubleshooting system discrepancies. Potential sources must be capable of and have access to Northrop Grumman equipment. Potential sources would need to have the ability to ensure equipment would be able to detect rain rates in real-time directly in front of the aircraft either proving or disproving the capability. The proposed services are required to have access to Northrop Grumman Corporation, and their databases which contain/maintain the APN-241 Radar System engineering software. The following equipment is required to sustain WC-130J RTP and will be provided as GFE: RTP P/N 780R270G10 (NSN 5841-01-522-1618), Transmitter Module (1A05) P/N 444R372G01 (NSN 5841-01-433-9455), and General-Purpose Processor Module P/N 824R061G06 (NSN 5998-01-534-5169). The modified configuration provided is the following equipment: WC-130J RTP P/N 780R270G13 (NSN 5841-01-546-5654), Transmitter Module (1A05) P/N 444R372G02 (NSN 6130-01-433-9452). And General- Purpose Processor Module P/N 824R061G13 (NSN 5998-01-564-1569). Provide sustaining engineering support and repairment of the modified configuration: WC-130J RTP P/N 780R270G13 (NSN 5841-01-546-5654), Transmitter Module (1A05) P/N 444R372G02 (NSN 6130-01-433-9452), and General-Purpose Processor Module P/N 824R061G13 (NSN 5998-01-564-1569) Provide engineering support during developmental testing not to exceed 400-man hours and provide on-site support at Eglin AFB for two engineers for a total of three 5-day trips. The proposed acquisition strategy is a 2-year (plus 6-month extension option) contract beginning in FY27 and continuing through FY29. The Government has determined this system is not a commercial item. There are no samples available for potential suppliers to evaluate. The Government anticipates this requirement to be sole source to: NORTHROP GRUMMAN CORPORATION (NGC) CAGE Code: 11982 4065 Colonel Glenn HWY Beavercreek Township, OH 45431 RFO 15.101 Early exchanges with industry As prescribed in 15.101(c), The government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this Request for Information or to otherwise pay for the information solicitated except as an allowable cost under other contracts as provided in subsection 31.205-18, Bid and proposal costs, of the Federal Acquisition Regulation Although �proposal� and �offeror are used in this Request for Information, your response will be treated as information only. title: Q522--On-site Board-Certified/Board-Eligible Diagnostic Radiology Physician Services | Orlando VA Healthcare System (OVAHCS)
description: Presolicitation Notice Presolicitation Notice Page 4 of 4 Presolicitation Notice *=Required Field Presolicitation Notice Page 1 of 4 The Department of Veterans Affairs, VISN 08, Orlando VA Healthcare System (OVAHCS), 13800 Veteran s Way, Orlando, FL 32827, intends to solicit an unrestricted full and open competitive Request for Proposals (RFP), to provide services necessary to perform two (2) Full Time Employee Equivalent (FTEE) on-site Board-Certified/Board-Eligible Diagnostic Radiology Physician Services (body imaging, Muscoskeletal (MSK) or Neuroradiology qualified) to eligible beneficiaries of the OVAHCS. The VA Radiology Services follow the standards & guidelines set forth by American College of Radiology (ACR). A contractor providing Diagnostic Radiology Physician Services shall provide services that meet or exceed the American College of Radiology Guidelines https://www.acr.org/-/media/ACR/Files/Practice-Parameters/IRClin-Prac-Mgmt.pdf.pdf. Two (2) Diagnostic Radiologists of differing subspecialties (one (1) Neuro and one (1) MSK; (1) Neuro and one (1) body; or one (1) MSK and one (1) body) are required to be onsite Monday Friday from 8:00am 4:30pm (30-minute lunch) excluding Federal Holidays (full-time basis). No off-hours coverage, on-call duties, or overtime are required. Each Diagnostic Radiologists must produce 9000 work Relative Value Units (wRVUs)/year (4.3 wRVUs/hour; 34.6 wRVUs/day). Qualified substitute personnel with credentials including board-certification/board-eligibility, comparable to designated key personnel must be fully credentialed and privileged and readily available to provide services in the event key personnel are unavailable. Given the importance of continuity of care to the Facility s medical services, the Contractor must maintain a contingency plan to ensure uninterrupted services if a physician departs employment or becomes unable to perform services and provide coverage. Contractor physicians must possess a minimum of three (3) years of continuous Board-Certified/Board-Eligible Diagnostic Radiologist experience within the last four (4) years, including demonstrated proficiency in interpreting Computed Tomography (CT), Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Ultrasound, and Diagnostic X-ray imaging. QUALIFICATIONS: License: The Contractor s physician(s) assigned by the Contractor to perform the services covered by this contract shall have a current license to practice medicine in any State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States or the District of Columbia) when services are performed onsite on VA property. All licenses held by the key personnel working on this contract shall be full and unrestricted licenses. Contractor s physician(s) who have current, full and unrestricted licenses in one or more states, but who have, or ever had, a license restricted, suspended, revoked, voluntarily revoked, voluntarily surrendered pending action or denied upon application will not be considered for the purposes of this contract. Board Certification: All contractor s physician(s) shall be Board-Certified /Board-Eligible per the American Board of Radiology (http://www.theabr.org/). All continuing education courses required for maintaining certification must be kept up to date at all times. Documentation verifying current certification shall be provided by the Contractor to the VA COR on an annual basis for each year of contract performance. Credentialing and Privileging: Credentialing and privileging is to be done in accordance with the provisions of VHA Directive 1100.20 and VHA Directive 1100.21 referenced above. The Contractor is responsible for ensuring that proposed physician(s) possesses the requisite credentials enabling the granting of privileges. No services shall be provided by any Contractor s physician(s) prior to obtaining approval by the Facility Medical Executive Board and Medical Center Director. The period of performance is expected to be from February 1, 2027, through January 31, 2032. The authority of for this procurement is Title 38 USC 8153, Health Care Resources (HCR) Sharing Authority, Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services, and RFO 15, Contracting by Negotiation. The solicitation document will be issued as Request for Proposals (RFP) 36C24827R0006 as an unrestricted open and competitive solicitation on or about November 2, 2026. Interested contractors will be responsible for downloading copies of the solicitation and any subsequent amendments from this website. No hard copies will be made available. The solicitation will provide instructions to contractors about the response to the RFP submission process. Prospective contractors are encouraged to register their interest in the solicitation on the SAM.gov | Contract Opportunities website so that they are notified of the issuance of the solicitation and any amendments. In accordance with RFO 52.204-7, System for Award Management (SAM), prospective contractors must be registered in SAM to be eligible for award. Contractors may obtain SAM information at https://sam.gov/. Registration is free and potential offerors are encouraged to visit the SAM website (SAM.gov | Entity Information). The NAICS Code for this procurement is 621111 Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists); Product/Service Code: Q522 Medical-Radiology. The Business Size Standard is $16 million. Any questions concerning this announcement should be directed to Jayne Messer, Contracting Officer, via electronic mail (email) at jayne.messer@va.gov and include the solicitation number on subject line (i.e., RFP 36C24827R0006).

When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. title: Maintenance, Repair and Preservation of YT-811
description: The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of YT-811. The YT-811 characteristics are Length: 90 FT, Width: 38FT 5IN, Age: 4 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 16 FT, Full Displacement: 494 L Tons and Light Load: 438 L Tons.The Contractors facility must possess the capability of YT-811 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. The Government will transport the vessel to the Contractors repair facility. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Replace zinc anodes. Blast and preserve underwater hull and freeboard, bulwarks, and handrails. Blast and preserve main deck, 1st deck, and 2nd deck non-skid, FME all polished stainless steel surfaces. Perform hull and freeboard Ultrasonic Test (UT) inspections. Perform hull and freeboard, main deck, 1st deck, and 2nd deck Visual Inspections (VT). Repair hull and winch valves. Repair deckhouse expansion joint. Test and preserve CHT, ballast, potable water, fuel oil, waste oil and day tanks. Accomplish Mast Lighting and Deckhouse Lighting Repairs. Replace all placards and labels on main, 1st and 2nd decks. Replace deck winch, mast, and brow systems hydraulic hoses. Accomplish winch control piping modification (YT-0104D). Overhaul Mast hydraulic ram, replace pins and bushings. Undock the vessel. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the SUPERVISOR. Upon completion of all work the Government will take custody of the vessel. Specific details of all work items and tasks required by this Statement of Work described in this Scope Overview are included in section 3.0 of this Statement of Work.The YT-811 will be ready for pick up on or after 2 March 2027. Refer to page 1 Request for Quote (RFQ) of the Solicitation regarding desired and required delivery information.This is full and open competition. All offerors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) to receive award of Government contracts. Offerors are advised also that SAM representations and certifications can be completed electronically via the System for Award Management website at https://www.sam.gov.

title: Market Intelligence Notice � Hangar Construction (Hybrid Conventional and Tension Fabric Structures)
description: Market Intelligence Notice � Hangar Construction (Hybrid Conventional and Tension Fabric Structures) Disclaimer: This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation or a commitment to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. 1.0 Objective The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Savannah District (SAS) is seeking market intelligence to identify and assess industry capabilities relevant to Tension Fabric Structures (TFS) and hybrid industrialized construction solutions for hangar facilities and similar large-span mission support applications. The Government is pursuing modern industrialized construction approaches intended to improve schedule, cost, and lifecycle outcomes for this facility type. Information provided by respondents will be used to help the Government understand available market participants, solution types, and industry interest, and will inform future industry engagements, acquisition planning, and assessment of potential use of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a, Facility Construction or Repair: Transactions Other Than Contracts and Grants. 2.0 Forecasted Projects - Overview The following projects are currently projected for potential TFS or hybrid industrialized construction applications. USACE, SAS requires a highly resilient, energy-efficient operational hangar facility that can be rapidly constructed, scaled, and reconfigured as a tension-fabric structure. Solutions may be scaled for additional hangar facilities identified later. Maintenance Hangar, Hunter Army Airfield (HAAF), GA (approximately 193,513 square footage (SF)). Construction of a Large (10 Module) Standard Design Aircraft Maintenance Hangar Complex with integrated aviation maintenance operations, maintenance support, company operations, flight planning, flight operations spaces, Ground Support Equipment (GSE) covered storage, Associated Support Items of Equipment (ASIOE) covered storage, Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants (POL) and Hazardous Material (HAZMAT) storage, hangar access and wash aprons. Project also includes fire protection and alarm systems, information systems, Intrusion Detection System (IDS) installation, closed circuit television connection, cybersecurity measures, and Energy Monitoring Control Systems (EMCS) connection. Supporting facilities include site development, utilities and connections, exterior lighting, paving, POV parking, walks, storm drainage, information systems, landscaping and signage. Heating and air conditioning will be provided by self-contained system. Moody Air Force Base, GA (approximately 105,000 SF). Construction of an adequately sized six-bay hangar and squadron operations facility. The squadron operations section of the facility shall incorporate mission planning, life support, and squadron admin space. The aircraft maintenance section shall be designed to optimize maintenance administration for the squadron. The hangar bays will provide space to support aircraft repair and inspection, engine changes, and other activities that must be accomplished in a secure, climate-controlled environment. The hangar space must be sized to accommodate movement and placement of maintenance equipment around the aircraft and systems supporting the aircraft. 3.0 Requested Information & Market Intelligence Questionnaire Section - General Information Provide responses to the survey linked herein. https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/8B5GPKqrMh Section - Capabilities Respondents are asked to structure Capability Statements to include the following elements: Corporate Overview - A brief summary of your firm's core capabilities, relevant experience, and capacity to perform the type of work contemplated under this RFI. Commercial Best Practices. To the extent available, provide information regarding commercial best practices applicable to the contemplated construction delivery method, including: Typical pricing/payment structures Geographic coverage Typical project schedule timelines, long lead items, and key decision points Key considerations and risk associated with permitting, logistics, staffing/labor availability, and construction execution. Specialized Systems Integration: Describe your experience integrating specialized hangar systems, such as high-capacity cranes, fall protection systems, and high-expansion foam fire suppression systems, within a tension fabric structure. Supply Chain and Logistics: Describe your supply chain for key components of the tension fabric structure. What are your typical lead times for material and fabrication? Materials and Durability: What specific materials, coatings, and structural frame materials do you typically use for facilities of this type and in a coastal environment? What is the expected design life and warranty period for these components? 3. Survey Responses � Please provide detailed responses to Survey Questions 10 through 12 (listed below and on the survey form). Respondents are asked to integrate these responses directly into their capability statements; separate or stand-alone survey responses are not required. Additional Information � Respondents may include other information that demonstrates their relevant capabilities, experience, and capacity. Examples include: Photos of TFS projects ; Smart Building Technologies (e.g., automated controls, sensors, energy management systems, fire protection and alarm systems, information systems, Intrusion Detection System (IDS) installation, closed circuit television connection, cybersecurity measures, and Energy Monitoring Control Systems (EMCS) connection.) Advanced HVAC Systems (e.g., high-efficiency climate control, specialized filtration) Survey Questions 10-12 10. Describe your experience or capability in designing and constructing tension-fabric structures that could innovate and accelerate construction. 11. Describe your firm�s practical experience with collaborative delivery models, such as Design-Build, Progressive Design-Build or Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR), where your team was integrated into the design phase. What specific pre-construction services did you provide? 12. For the projects listed in response to Q11, identify the major subcontractor(s) used and describe their qualifications. Detail the teaming relationship and contract structure between the construction contractor, the owner, and the Designer of Record. Explain how your team's involvement improved the final design quality, accelerated the delivery schedule, and reduced overall project cost. 4.0 Response Submission Instructions Format: Responses to the survey must be submitted via the link provided. The capability statement must be submitted in PDF format, single-spaced, using 11-point font or larger. Submission Deadline: October 23, 2026 � 5:00 PM Submission Channel: Complete the survey at https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/8B5GPKqrMh Submit capability statement via email to the Agreement Officer (AO) at Jennifer.L.Murphy@usace.army.mil and copy Sabrina.Bastine@usace.army.mil with the subject line: "USACE OTA Market Intelligence Response TFS - [Company Name]". Proprietary Information: Any proprietary, sensitive, or business-confidential information must be clearly marked as such on each page to ensure proper handling by USACE SAS.

title: HPCMP Innovative Technology Insertion of Advanced HPC Systems Commercial Solutions Openings (CSO)
description: The Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC) is issuing a Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) pursuant to DFARS Subpart 212.70. Under a CSO, the ERDC may competitively award proposals received in response to a general solicitation, similar to a Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), to acquire innovative commercial products, technologies, or services based on a review of solutions by scientific, technological, or other subject matter expert peers within the ERDC. �Innovative,� for CSO purposes, means any new technology, process, or method, including research and development (R&D), or any new application of an existing technology, process, or method. Under this CSO, all products, technologies, and services shall be treated as commercial items; products, technologies, and services do not have to be �commercially available� to be submitted in response to this solicitation. If the solution meets the requirements of the regulation, the solution is treated as commercial whereby the Contracting Officer will utilize commercial procedures to develop and execute the resultant award. The DoW High Performance Computing Modernization Program (HPCMP) is seeking innovative solutions to establish a new high-performance computing (HPC) system acquisition and support services model that leverages industry best practices to transform how the HPCMP procures, operates, and maintains its newest HPC systems for 2027. The HPC systems being considered are a combination of compute-intensive architectures and artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) platforms operating in either unclassified or classified (secret and above-secret) environments. The systems would be geographically distributed at up to three of the five HPCMP DoW Supercomputing Resource Centers (DSRCs). Since the systems will reside on-premises in the DSRCs, the services model must also conform to DoW and local Service policies, especially regarding security (physical, personnel, and cyber). To navigate the current market conditions and meet mission objectives, a new strategy is needed to design, manufacture, deliver, install, operate and maintain one or more HPC systems at one to three different HPC centers. The anticipated systems will be a combination of compute-intensive architectures (mostly CPU-based) and artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) platforms (mostly GPU-based) operating in either unclassified or classified (secret and above-secret) environments. Go to https://www.erdcwerx.org/innovative-technology-insertion-of-advanced-hpc-systems/ for all of the CSO details and submission requirements. All solutions must be submitted through the ERDCWERX platform. The ERDC may award a FAR-based contract or an Other Transaction under this announcement. All resultant FAR-based contracts will be firm-fixed price. All items, technologies, and services (including research and development) procured via this CSO are treated as commercial. Applicants from universities and/or non-profit organizations should be aware that commercial clauses will be integrated into the award and should coordinate proposals with associated legal counsel prior to submission.

title: Request for Information: United States Coast Guard Core Navigation Software
description: Description & Purpose of Request 1.1 Objective The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is conducting market research in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 to identify commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) and Non-Developmental Item (NDI) core maritime navigation software solutions that have the capability of being enhanced to meet USCG requirements (e.g. EAIS IDD). The primary objective is to survey industry capabilities to inform the prospective modernization and eventual replacement of the legacy USCG �Vega� navigation software suite (currently derived from commercial core navigation architectures) across the cutter and boat fleet. 1.2 Purpose & Scope of Market Inquiry The Coast Guard seeks insight into the current commercial and naval navigation software, including cutting-edge display engines, autonomous voyage planning, sensor fusion, resilient Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), and modern software architectures (e.g., modular open systems, containerized microservices, cross-platform runtimes). The Government intends to assess software suites that can match or exceed the complete operational baseline of current USCG E-NAV capabilities while remaining flexible, open, and capable of integrating seamlessly into existing USCG shipboard hardware configurations without requiring complete bridge refits. 1.3 Disclaimer This is a Request for Information (RFI) and is issued solely for informational, market research, and planning purposes. This is not a Request for Proposals or a Request for Quotations, and it is not considered to be a commitment by the Government to award a contract/order nor is the Government responsible for any costs incurred in furnishing information provided under this RFI. No basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this RFI or Government use of any information provided. Further, the Government is not seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited proposals at this time. No classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response to this RFI. Proprietary information must be clearly marked if included. The Government reserves the right to use any information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate, including using technical information provided by respondents in any resultant solicitation. Responses will assist the Government in determining the availability of potential solutions and commercial products in the market. At this time, no solicitation exists; therefore, please do not request a copy of the solicitation. The information and requirements in this RFI, and any attachments, is subject to change at the sole discretion of the Government. 2. Operational Environment & Hardware Baseline Constraints To ensure candidate software solutions can integrate into active cutter classes without widespread structural or electrical bridge overhauls, respondents must demonstrate compatibility with the following operational constraints: 2.1 Installed Hardware Baseline (E-NAV) The USCG fleet operates on a variety of IEC 60945 compliant hardware baselines consisting of: rack mounted industrial computers, rack mounted servers, ruggedized small factor computers, marine-grade All-in-One (AIO) Computer/Displays, system displays ranging from 15-19 inches, KVM matrix, ruggedized mouse and keyboard. 2.2 Operating System (OS) Gatekeeper Requirements Software architecture must natively support modern enterprise operating system standards: Microsoft Windows 11 Enterprise (including Long-Term Servicing Channel [LTSC] builds). Enterprise Linux Distributions (e.g., Latest version of Red Hat Enterprise Linux [RHEL]). Vendors must state whether their software executes natively on Windows 11, Linux, or maintains a dual-OS cross-platform compiled codebase. 2.3 System Availability and Deterministic State Recovery Deterministic State Recovery: In the event of ungraceful bridge power interruption or system reset, the software must reboot and restore its previous operational state, active route, safety parameters, and sensor assignments without manual database rebuilding. 3. Core Functional Capability Matrix See Attachment. 3.1 Sensor Ingestion & Data Distribution Protocol Support: Native ingestion, parsing, translation, and broadcast of NMEA 0183, NMEA 2000 (IEC 61162-3), NMEA OneNet, and Lightweight Ethernet (LWE)(IEC 61162-450) protocols. Sensor Interfacing: Interfacing with gyrocompasses, Doppler velocity logs (DVL), magnetic compasses, wind sensors, depth sounders, GPS/DGPS/Galileo receivers, Inertial Navigation Systems (INS), and radar targets (ARPA). Integrity & Checksum: Cryptographic and checksum integrity verification for all data streams; automated detection and notification of malformed or invalid sentences. Decoupled Time Distribution: Network time distribution via UDP/TCP; ability to assign an authoritative UTC time source independent of the primary positioning source. 3.2 Data Recording, Playback, and Forensics Comprehensive Logging: Continuous background recording of ownship dynamics, sensor inputs, target tracking data, alert histories, and operator interactions. Storage Flexibility: Ability to write logs and telemetry to internal storage, external mission media (USB/NAS), or enterprise shipboard repositories. Visual Playback: Integrated forensic playback mode providing time-synchronized replay of chart presentation, radar overlay, and sensor states for accident investigation and tactical debrief. 3.3 Chart Management & Next-Gen Hydrographic Standards Legacy Format Support: Seamless handling of S-57 ENC, S-63 encrypted charts, and DNC (Digital Nautical Chart) formats. S-100 Transition Framework: Implementation roadmap and readiness for the IHO S-100 Universal Hydrographic Data Model, specifically: S-101 Electronic Navigational Charts (ENC) S-102 High-Resolution Bathymetric Surfaces S-104 Water Level Information S-111 Surface Currents S-124 Navigational Warnings Manual Corrections: Ability to create, save, import, and visually verify manual notice-to-mariners chart corrections and local marine hazards. 3.4 Operational Display Area (ODA) & Ownship Dynamics Ownship Dynamics: Multi-source position fixing utilizing GNSS (GGA/GNS), INS, Radar Chart Matching, manual visual/radar Lines of Position (LOPs), and Dead Reckoning (DR). Dynamic Calculations: Automated computation of real-time Set and Drift, Course Over Ground (COG), Speed Over Ground (SOG), Speed Through Water (STW), and Rate of Turn (ROT). Tactical Plotting: Rapid generation of Danger Bearings/Ranges, Clearing Lines, Variable Range Markers (VRM), Electronic Bearing Lines (EBL), and instant Man Overboard (MOB) emergency markers. RADAR Overlay: Software must be compatible with Furuno SDK and SSR COMRIC for RADAR overlay capability. 3.5 Human-System Interface (HSI) & Publications Visual Standards: Full conformance with IHO S-52 Presentation Library colors, symbology, and display modes (Day, Dusk, Night). Coordinate Precision: Coordinate calculation and display capabilities resolving latitude and longitude to one thousandth of a second (0.001�). Nautical Nomenclature: Standardization using Pub. 9 (Bowditch) and Chart No. 1 nautical symbology and abbreviations. Electronic Publications: Native viewer for hydrographic reference materials, Standard Bearing Books, and Adobe PDF navigation documentation. 3.6 Cybersecurity, Information Assurance & System Management DoD/DHS Compliance: Architecture capable of being hardened to DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs), meeting NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 security controls, and aligning with Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) parameters. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Distinct cryptographic user/administrator profiles, group policies, and role permissions preserved across software patches and upgrades. title: Maintenance, Repair and Preservation of YT-811
description: The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of YT-811. The YT-811 characteristics are Length: 90 FT, Width: 38FT 5IN, Age: 4 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 16 FT, Full Displacement: 494 L Tons and Light Load: 438 L Tons. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of YT-811 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. The Government will transport the vessel to the Contractors repair facility. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Replace zinc anodes. Blast and preserve underwater hull and freeboard, bulwarks, and handrails. Blast and preserve main deck, 1st deck, and 2nd deck non-skid, FME all polished stainless steel surfaces. Perform hull and freeboard Ultrasonic Test (UT) inspections. Perform hull and freeboard, main deck, 1st deck, and 2nd deck Visual Inspections (VT). Repair hull and winch valves. Repair deckhouse expansion joint. Test and preserve CHT, ballast, potable water, fuel oil, waste oil and day tanks. Accomplish Mast Lighting and Deckhouse Lighting Repairs. Replace all placards and labels on main, 1st and 2nd decks. Replace deck winch, mast, and brow systems hydraulic hoses. Accomplish winch control piping modification (YT-0104D). Overhaul Mast hydraulic ram, replace pins and bushings. Undock the vessel. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the SUPERVISOR. Upon completion of all work the Government will take custody of the vessel. Specific details of all work items and tasks required by this Statement of Work described in this Scope Overview are included in section 3.0 of this Statement of Work. The YT-811 will be ready for pick up on or after 2 March 2027. Refer to page 1 Request for Quote (RFQ) of the Solicitation regarding desired and required delivery information. This is full and open competition. All offerors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) to receive award of Government contracts. Offerors are advised also that SAM representations and certifications can be completed electronically via the System for Award Management website at https://www.sam.gov.

title: Copie Accompagnement du maître d'ouvrage pour la gare de Marin-Epagnier
description:
Présentation du projet – Module 1 : Construction de la nouvelle gare de Marin-Epagnier

La gare de Marin-Epagnier, située sur la ligne Berne – Neuchâtel, nécessite d’importants travaux de rénovation. Les installations destinées au public ne répondent pas aux exigences de la loi sur l’égalité des personnes handicapées ni à la norme relative à la longueur utile des quais. Dans le cadre de ce projet, la gare doit être réaménagée pour devenir un pôle de transport conforme aux normes, avec deux quais extérieurs, une longueur utile de quais de 220 m et un nouveau passage souterrain pour piétons.


Étendue des prestations - Module 1

Le chef de projet général « Construction » est responsable de la conception technique de tous les travaux relatifs aux voies ferrées, aux routes et aux travaux de génie civil (y compris les systèmes de drainage, les ouvrages d'art et les structures porteuses).

Le mandat comprend les phases suivantes, conformément à l'art. 3.2 du Règlement SIA 103/2020 :

- Phase 31 : avant-projet

- Phase 32 : projet de construction (option)

- Phase 33 : procédure d’autorisation / projet soumis à l’enquête publique (option)

- Phase 41 : appel d’offres, comparaison des offres, proposition d’attribution (option)

- Phase 51 : projet d’exécution (option)

- Phase 52 : exécution (öBL facultatif) (option)

- Phase 53 : Mise en service, clôture (option)


Conformément aux articles 3.3 et 3.4 du Règlement SIA 103/2020, le soumissionnaire prend en charge les tâches relevant des domaines de la direction générale, de la conception technique et de la direction des travaux (option). La direction générale des travaux ne fait pas partie du mandat. La BLS se réserve le droit d’assurer elle-même la direction des travaux du projet.

Les prestations des services spécialisés et de leurs mandataires doivent être coordonnées dans le temps avec ses propres prestations spécialisées (programme de travail coordonné). Les heures d'honoraires pour les phases 32 à 53 ont été estimées par le maître d'ouvrage et ne peuvent être modifiées dans le cadre de l'appel d'offres. Elles feront l'objet d'une nouvelle estimation à la fin de l'avant-projet. À l'issue de l'avant-projet, le maître d'ouvrage se réserve le droit de modifier l'organisation du projet. (Option)


Présentation du projet – Module 2 : remplacement du poste d’aiguillage de Marin-Epagnier

Dans le cadre du projet de rénovation de la gare et de mise en conformité avec la LHand, le renouvellement du poste d’aiguillage est prévu à Marin-Epagnier. Compte tenu de l’augmentation du volume de manœuvres sur le site, une mise en service anticipée du nouveau poste d’aiguillage d’ici 2030 permettra d’améliorer la sécurité d’exploitation dès que possible. L’installation de signaux nains permettra de mieux sécuriser les manœuvres et d’améliorer considérablement le niveau de sécurité dans l’exploitation quotidienne.


Étendue des prestations du module 2

title: Germany – Architectural and related services – Objektplanungsleistungen für Gebäude und Innenräume nach Teil 3 Abschnitt 1 HOAI, Vorabmaßnahmen am NWZ I für die Sanierung von NWZ II
description: Universität Stuttgart; NWZ II, Sanierung für Chemie, Objektplanungsleistungen für Gebäude und Innenräume nach Teil 3 Abschnitt 1 HOAI, Vorabmaßnahmen am NWZ I für die Sanierung von NWZ II, Pfaffenwaldring 55, 70569 Stuttgart, Das Naturwissenschaftliche Zentrum (NWZ) I und II im Pfaffenwaldring (PWR) 55 und 57 wurde in den 1970er Jahren fertiggestellt. Das NWZ soll in den kommenden Jahren abschnittsweise generalsaniert werden. Sanierungsabschnitt 1 betrifft das NWZ II, während Sanierungsabschnitt 2 das NWZ I betrifft. Die in diesem Verfahren ausgeschriebenen Planungsaufgaben sind die Vorabmaßnahmen am NWZ I im Vorgriff auf die geplante Sanierung des NWZ II im ersten Sanierungsabschnitt. Sie sind Teil der Gesamtsanierungsmaßnahme NWZ. Es müssen diverse Anpassungsmaßnahmen am NWZ I erfolgen, um die beiden Gebäude seitens des Hochbaus und der Gebäudetechnik zu entflechten und abzutrennen. Zudem müssen bisherige Nutzungen aus dem NWZ II für dessen Sanierung interimsweise im NWZ I untergebracht und dort vorhandene Nutzungen verdichtet werden. Im Laborhochhaus des NWZ I (PWR 55) mit östlich angrenzenden Flachbauten ist die die Fakultät Chemie untergebracht. In den Flachbauten sind Hörsäle, die Universitätsbibliothek und eine Cafeteria verortet. Das NWZ I verfügt über insgesamt 23.800 m² NUF (1-6). Die zur Beauftragung vorgesehenen Objektplanungsleistungen beziehen sich auf Teilflächen des Gebäudes mit ca. 2.900 m² NUF und umfassen im Wesentlichen die Arbeiten an: Bibliothek mit ca. 2.520 m² NUF, Verwaltungs- und Fachschaftsflächen mit ca. 90 m² NUF sowie Praktika- und Laborflächen mit ca. 290 m² NUF. Die Maßnahme beinhaltet zudem Arbeiten an betriebsrelevanten Ver- und Entsorgungsanlagen wie z.B. Anlagen für technische Gase und Abwasserbehandlung. Das Gebäude befindet sich größtenteils im Errichtungszustand mit entsprechenden bauzeitlichen Schadstoffbelastungen. Bei den Maßnahmenhandelt es sich um Interimslösungen bis zur geplanten Inbetriebnahme des NWZ II und der Generalsanierung des NWZ I. Das Gebäude befindet sich in der Campusmitte innerhalb einer dichten/beengten städtebaulichen Struktur. Die Umsetzung erfolgt im regulären Universitäts-/Gebäudebetrieb. Kosten: Die Bauwerkskosten (KG 300-400) betragen ca. 8.000.000 Euro brutto. Nicht berücksichtigt sind hierbei die Kosten für mögliche Baupreis- und Bauherrenrisiken. Termine: Der Projektstart ist Ende Januar mit der Auftragserteilung terminiert. Abschluss der LPH 2 ist im März 2027 geplant und hinsichtlich der Gesamtterminschiene zwingend erforderlich. Fertigstellung der Maßnahme ist im 1. Quartal 2031 vorgesehen. Objektplanungsleistungen für Gebäude und Innenräume nach Teil 3 Abschnitt 1 HOAI nach Teil 3 Abschnitt 1 HOAI, Grundleistungen der Leistungsphasen 2 bis 9 nach § 34 HOAI sowie Besondere Leistungen der Leistungsphase 2.

This procurement is for Non-Emergent Medical Transportation (NEMT) services and was conducted in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 12 Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. In accordance with RFO 12.102, Restricting Competition for the acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services requires a justification using the format as described in RFO 6.104-1. A sole source, short term, six (6) week emergency contract is essential to provide vital healthcare services for Veterans at PVAHCS. This requirement ensures continued access to critical healthcare services while the long-term contract is competitively solicited. This requirement was awarded as a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. Non-Emergent Medical Transportation services are required by statute under 38 USC 111A. Services include pre-arranged, scheduled, unscheduled, and will call door-to-door service from beneficiary�s apartments and homes, and other areas designated by the Patient Travel Office (PTO) to get to and from scheduled medical appointments. It also includes discharges from PVAHCS inpatient wards, the Emergency Department, as well as transports to and from contracted nursing homes. This short-term bridge contract is needed to ensure regulatory compliance and continuity of mission critical services for 6 weeks, pending the award and performance start date of the competively solicited long-term contract.

title: Alternative Fuels & Feedstock Initiative to Add Value to Seed Oil Crops through Improved Preprocessing, Scalability, and Valorization of Product Streams
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from prospective offerors to complement existing seed oil crop research efforts at the Biomass Feedstock National User Facility (BFNUF) through U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) funded work. Appropriate topics of research will develop a greater understanding of harvesting, storage, separations, and scalability that increase the value of seed oil crops by reducing processing costs, increasing yields, and/or generating material streams that can be valorized. Topics that are not of interest to this EOI include operations upstream of harvesting (e.g., agronomy, crop engineering, genetic engineering), and downstream of processing (e.g., new conversion technologies). This effort expects to fund a maximum of two projects through DOE�s Alternative Fuels & Feedstock Office (AFFO). Projects can be led by industry or a U.S. university, with INL collaboration. BACKGROUND AFFO and Idaho National Laboratory (INL) seek research that improves post?harvest preprocessing, storage, separations, and scalable fractionation of seed oil crops to reduce costs, increase yields, and create valuable non?oil product streams. Work must focus on post?harvest operations and demonstrate scalability. Awardees will collaborate with INL�s BFNUF and generate data supporting an INL?led technoeconomic assessment (TEA) SCOPE OF WORK BEA is seeking qualified company or U.S University to support the BFNUF and AFFO mission through novel research that increases the value of seed oil crops through more effective harvesting, storage, fractionation, and/or valorization for seed components. If the proposed work is bench-scale, a case must be made for why it is scalable to field applications. Proposed research may focus on commodity or niche seed oil crops. More niche seed feedstocks will be considered if the research team can demonstrate the extent to which the proposed methods are broadly applicable. EOIs should focus on the non-oil components of the seed, although outcomes affecting the oil extraction process can be considered in the overall potential impact of the proposed work. The winning project team will collaborate with INL and help design INL scope that uses BFNUF capabilities, which may be reviewed at Biomass Feedstock National User Facility - Idaho National Laboratory. Qualifications for successful applicants include: Technical Expertise and Leadership: Strong technical credentials and experience, demonstrated by impactful research publications. There will be a preference for teams with experience collaborating with industrial partners or in performing industrially relevant research. Collaboration and Networking: Demonstrated ability to work with and lead teams from different organizations. Industry and Workforce Development Connections: Extensive ties with agricultural companies, equipment manufacturers, and/or energy sectors. Interested applicants will propose scope to address the research challenge posed. It is anticipated that the project duration will be between 12 and 24 months and will support approximately 0.25 FTEs for project PI and 1.0 � 3.0 FTEs for technicians/post docs/students. In addition to labor, the project may include laboratory consumables commensurate with the proposed scope. Any non-consumable equipment purchases, or planned travel must be specified in the proposed scope and is subject to approval by INL. Project resources required to fund BEA and BFNUF activities are separate from the awarded amount, which will be managed through a contract with BEA. As determined by BEA, responders to this EOI may receive a Request for Proposal (RFP) that may require detailed technical and price proposals for evaluation and ranking in a selection process. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested individuals are requested to email expressions of interest to BFNUF@inl.gov and chase.egbert@inl.gov by 6PM Mountain Standard Time on October 23, 2026. Included must be sufficient written information confirming the responder�s qualifications, including the following: � For all core team members (no page limit): Name Institution Contact Information CV or Resume � A brief statement (no more than three - five pages in length) including: The objective of the planned proposed work The approach to meeting the research objective The scale and technology readiness level of the proposed work Team members, resources, and roles for each team member How the team will collaborate with the BFNUF and include an INL-led TEA Expressions of interest may be submitted by 1) Contacting BFNUF@inl.gov to receive a link to securely transmit your application using Box, or 2) Emailed directly to BFNUF@inl.gov and chase.egbert@inl.gov. If you do the latter, please enable encryption features in your email platform to ensure secure transmission. Securely sending emails protects sensitive information from unauthorized access. Transmitting PII via non-secured methods carries inherent risks for which you are accountable. Only potentially qualified offerors, as determined by BEA, will be contacted for further discussions or the release of a request for proposal for the project. Interested individuals are advised that the selection decision is anticipated in January 2027. If you have questions, need additional information, or need to speak with a BEA subject matter expert for clarification, please email BFNUF@inl.gov. For further questions regarding BFNUF capabilities, please reach out via email at BFNUF@inl.gov. Proposing teams should anticipate collecting information that will support a technoeconomic assessment completed by INL. Deadline for submission:?October 23, 2026 Submit to:?Chase.Egbert@inl.gov and BFNUF@inl.gov PROPRIETARY INFORMATION Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents must mark information in their responses accordingly.
